identification: Readable, unversioned EDRSilencer technique reconstructions in C#, C++ and Rust, not evidence of byte-identical upstream releases.
judgment: The code specifically selects SentinelAgent.exe and CylanceSvc.exe, derives an ALE application ID from each selected path, and uses that ID as an equality condition on outbound IPv4 and IPv6 BLOCK filters. Deliberately isolating security agents from their servers tips the balance toward malicious use, even where filter validation should prevent success.
counterevidence_and_context: Representative/reconstruction comments and public source distribution fit education or authorized offensive testing. No authorization, original registry package/version, surrounding article, build configuration, or deployment history was supplied. Source possession alone does not establish compromise. Judgment concerns the implemented agent-silencing capability; no malicious registry release attribution is asserted.
common_trace: Open the local WFP engine using current credentials, RPC_C_AUTHN_DEFAULT, and a null session pointer.
Select only the two security-agent basenames, case insensitively; unrelated images are skipped.
Resolve the image filename through FwpmGetAppIdFromFileName0. Failed resolutions skip the image.
Store the returned blob in an equality condition on FWPM_CONDITION_ALE_APP_ID.
Set BLOCK action and attempt FwpmFilterAdd0 at both ALE_AUTH_CONNECT_V4 and V6.
Free the application-ID buffer and close the engine. No filter-deletion call is present.
execution_limits: Reviewed every statement and relevant branch in each original source; did not compile or execute Windows security-policy modifications. Generated C# bindings, Rust dependency versions, and original build manifests are absent.

FWPM_FILTER0.displayData.name is required. C# default initialization and Rust zero initialization leave it null, so these filter additions are expected to fail validation; both ignore the return codes. Existing hostile descriptions correctly say attempts.

A null session is not dynamic: successfully added objects are not automatically deleted by engine closure. No FWPM_FILTER_FLAG_PERSISTENT is set, so no survival across BFE restart or reboot is claimed.

No process termination, injection, driver installation, privilege escalation, credential access, exfiltration, payload acquisition, C2 channel, or durable code reactivation exists in the supplied source.
obfuscation: None. Facts report no non-RawScan/decoded strings and no archive members. Rust UTF-16 conversion prepares the Windows API filename and is not concealment.
coverage_gap: Both retained hostile findings describe the same EDR network-blocking technique at different name-count thresholds. They are not two distinct hostile outcomes. C# and C++ process inventory/path lookup are already covered by notable capability traits. Rust has no process enumeration, only a caller-supplied path slice. No additional hostile or suspicious outcomes are supported; none were invented to meet trait-count guidance.

trait_change.evidence: Parsed call path.encode_utf16 at byte 826; appends a zero code unit and passes wide.as_ptr() to FwpmGetAppIdFromFileName0.
trait_change.placement: A directional character-encoding operation belongs in micro-behaviors/data/encode/charset, the existing admitted leaf, rather than anti-static or metadata.
trait_change.weakening_or_removal: None. No existing YAML rule or consumer changed. No whole-directory consumers of data/encode or data/encode/charset were found; an existing XOR consumer names the separate dotnet-utf8-getbytes atom explicitly.

samples.trace: Main enumerates Process.GetProcesses, compares ProcessName + .exe, and reads each selected MainModule.FileName. V6 then V4 filter additions are attempted regardless of their status. The missing display name prevents assuming success; unhandled process-access exceptions may stop enumeration.

samples.trace: main snapshots processes, iterates Process32FirstA/Process32NextA, opens only selected PIDs with PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, and queries full image paths. install adds V4, returns immediately if that call fails, then tries V6. The caller ignores the helper result. It supplies a display name and default FWP_EMPTY weight; no cleanup/rollback of an added V4 filter is implemented.
